A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching methods, eight card games and core experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, learning curves, cross-game transfer results and general-capability evaluations in Section 4, Tables 2–3 and Figures 2–7.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds role-specific results, model comparisons, transfer analyses and recovery evaluations in the main text and Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The trajectory generation and filtering, game prompts, JSON actions, LoRA fine-tuning, mixed-game training and subsequent general-data recovery procedure remain unchanged. All eight appendix prompt templates match after removing formatting differences.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 expands general-capability evaluation from three benchmarks to seven, adding GQPA-Diamond (the PDF's spelling), AIME2024, LiveCodeBench and IFEval. This includes previously untested instruction-following capability. The eight evaluated card games remain unchanged; Chess and Go appear only as contextual additions to Figure 1.

E2.justification: DeepSeek-R1 is added to the evaluated API-model comparison in v3 Table 3, corresponding to v1 Table 2. The five original API comparators, base-model comparators and game opponents are retained.

E3.justification: Existing training budgets, hyperparameters, opponents and evaluation game counts remain unchanged. Added evaluations extend cross-game testing to Llama and GLM, assess game performance before and after general-data recovery, and report a seven-benchmark average. Detailed evaluation settings for the additional general benchmarks are not supplied.

E4.justification: v3 adds a landlord/farmer breakdown investigating the 14B model's weakness (Table 2), extends transfer analysis beyond Qwen to Llama and GLM (Tables 5–6), and tests whether general-capability recovery preserves gaming performance (Table 7). Appendix A.2 additionally examines recovery across broader capabilities, revealing instruction-following degradation.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies training-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new checklist explicitly explains that error bars were omitted because of computational expense, but does not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in Tables 2, 3 and 5–8, while shared original scores are retained. DeepSeek-R1 leads the expanded API comparison on three games. Newly reported recovery results include Llama's Riichi score falling from 1.38 to 1.08 and IFEval scores falling from 74.31 to 68.95 for Llama and 63.40 to 56.01 for GLM.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical results, formal assumptions, proofs or derivations. Existing game descriptions and information-set explanations remain substantively unchanged; the additional empirical analyses do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claim that LLMs can 'master multiple complex card games simultaneously' to achieving 'a certain level of proficiency' in them. The main contributions and conclusion otherwise remain substantially unchanged, and stronger mastery wording persists in the introduction and results.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the 14B overfitting conjecture with a role-specific explanation supported by its weaker farmer performance. It adds interpretations that reasoning benefits DeepSeek-R1 and that recovery largely preserves gaming skill. Appendix A.2 materially qualifies recovery by arguing that capabilities absent from recovery data are not restored, citing instruction-following declines. The separate limitations section remains substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code link in the abstract and states in its checklist that usage and licensing information are provided in the repository. Existing hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, training times and prompt templates are retained. The PDFs alone do not verify the repository's contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to BALROG and LmAct when discussing evaluations without fine-tuning. The related-work discussion and positioning around learning complex games remain otherwise unchanged. Switching to numbered references and updating bibliographic metadata do not constitute additional positioning changes.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained. Changes include localized abstract and analysis revisions, expanded captions, standardized model names, numbered citations, updated affiliation and conference information, acknowledgements, a NeurIPS checklist and a new appendix subsection.

P2.justification: v3 introduces five tables covering role performance, two additional transfer matrices, game retention and expanded general benchmarks. Table 8 also redisplays existing Figure 7 results. Figure 1 adds Chess, Go and a perfect/imperfect-information legend; existing tables gain clearer captions and ranking emphasis, and several figures are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v1 evaluated general-task recovery without reporting subsequent game performance; v3 Table 7 fills that gap, while Table 8 exposes recovery limitations and Table 2 improves the 14B diagnosis. These strengthen the evidence. However, new Tables 5–6 give single-game GuanDan scores of 0.598/0.629 while retained Figure 5 shows 0.639/0.668, without explaining different settings, and uncertainty estimates remain absent. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
